summary:
Every rating in the model is pointing the same direction today, which almost never happens this late in the year with only one game on the board. R1 through R4 all land on MIL at LAD, with deltas clustering tight between -0.81 and -1.06 — that's as clean a consensus as you'll see, and it's backed by category strength, not just rating alignment. Hitting is the hottest cell across the board right now: R4 hitting sits at 72% (18-7, n=25) over a 52% season mark, R3 and R2 hitting are both at 68% (17-8), and R1 hitting is 60% (+9.3pts) — all carrying 3-game losing streaks that make tonight a bounce-back spot rather than a fade. Bullpen and bullpen_fatigue are riding similar heat across all four ratings (56-60% last 14, +5.6 to +10.6pts), so any rating leaning on pen metrics for this one is trustworthy. The one red flag is starting pitching — every single rating is cold on SP, 40% last 14 (10-15) with an identical 8-game losing streak across R1-R4. With Snell on the mound for LAD and Gasser for MIL, don't let an SP-driven signal talk you out of the consensus; let hitting and bullpen carry the read instead.

The team trends reinforce the lean: LAD is 39-17 (70%) when picked this season and a blistering 28-7 (80%, +27.0u) on strong plays, the best "team-when-liked" profile in the sample — but today the model's picking against them, toward MIL, which is itself 45-22 (67%, n=67) and 26-12 (68%, +17.0u) on strong plays, arguably the second-best team profile in the table. That's a case of two high-quality team signals colliding, and the rating consensus plus hot hitting/bullpen categories should break the tie toward MIL. On the unit side, R3 remains the hottest rating lately — 30d 34-15 (69%, +21.0u) and season +90.0u, the best net of the four — so if you're sizing today's single game, lean hardest on R3's number. R1 and R2 are both in modest 7-day dips (-1.0u and -2.0u on tiny samples), but that's noise against the 30-day trend, not a signal to fade the consensus.
